description: Pi-hole-style view of Blocky's query log out of Loki: who is asking, what is blocked, and what is served from cache rather than resolved.

panels.title: Queries
panels.description: Every query the selected resolver(s) answered in the dashboard time range, after the client filter.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` [$__range]))

panels.title: Blocked
panels.description: Queries answered from a blocklist rather than resolved.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} |= "BLOCKED" | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason =~ `BLOCKED.*` [$__range]))

panels.title: Block rate
panels.description: Blocked as a share of all queries.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} |= "BLOCKED" | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason =~ `BLOCKED.*` [$__range])) / sum(count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` [$__range])) * 100

panels.title: Served from cache
panels.description: Share of the queries that actually needed an answer (i.e. excluding blocked ones) that Blocky served from its own cache instead of asking anything upstream. CACHED NEGATIVE counts as a hit.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} |= "CACHED" | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason =~ `CACHED.*` [$__range])) / sum(count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason !~ `BLOCKED.*` [$__range])) * 100

panels.title: Clients
panels.description: Distinct client names seen in the range.

targets.expr: count(sum by (client_name) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` [$__range])))

panels.title: p95 lookup
panels.description: 95th percentile of Blocky's own duration column, over real lookups only — blocked and cached answers are 0 ms and would flatter it.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, {job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason !~ `BLOCKED.*` | reason !~ `CACHED.*` | unwrap duration_ms [$__range]) by ()

panels.title: Where answers came from
panels.description: Every query bucketed by what actually produced the answer. 'Cached' and 'Recursive (Unbound)' are the two that matter for cache-vs-real-lookup: anything that is not cached, blocked or conditional left the house. 'Upstream DoH (fallback)' should normally be empty — Blocky's upstream strategy is `strict`, so traffic only lands there when Unbound is failing, and a persistent band is worth chasing.

targets.expr: sum by (source) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | label_format source=`{{ if hasPrefix "BLOCKED" .reason }}Blocked{{ else if hasPrefix "CACHED" .reason }}Cached{{ else if eq .reason "CONDITIONAL" }}Conditional (UDM Pro){{ else if hasPrefix "RESOLVED (tcp+udp:127.0.0.1:5335)" .reason }}Recursive (Unbound){{ else if hasPrefix "RESOLVED (https" .reason }}Upstream DoH (fallback){{ else if hasPrefix "RESOLVED" .reason }}Resolved (other upstream){{ else if hasPrefix "CUSTOM DNS" .reason }}Custom DNS{{ else if hasPrefix "Special-Use" .reason }}Special-use (RFC 6761){{ else }}{{ .reason }}{{ end }}` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Answer source mix
panels.description: The same breakdown totalled over the range.

targets.expr: sum by (source) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | label_format source=`{{ if hasPrefix "BLOCKED" .reason }}Blocked{{ else if hasPrefix "CACHED" .reason }}Cached{{ else if eq .reason "CONDITIONAL" }}Conditional (UDM Pro){{ else if hasPrefix "RESOLVED (tcp+udp:127.0.0.1:5335)" .reason }}Recursive (Unbound){{ else if hasPrefix "RESOLVED (https" .reason }}Upstream DoH (fallback){{ else if hasPrefix "RESOLVED" .reason }}Resolved (other upstream){{ else if hasPrefix "CUSTOM DNS" .reason }}Custom DNS{{ else if hasPrefix "Special-Use" .reason }}Special-use (RFC 6761){{ else }}{{ .reason }}{{ end }}` [$__range]))

panels.title: Blocked vs allowed
panels.description: The headline split over time, for whatever the host and client pickers currently select.

targets.expr: sum by (status) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | label_format status=`{{ if hasPrefix "BLOCKED" .reason }}Blocked{{ else }}Allowed{{ end }}` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Blocked vs allowed, by resolver
panels.description: Per DNS host. These are two independent resolvers, not a cluster — a client configured with both appears in both, so the two bars are not shares of one pie.

targets.expr: sort_desc(sum by (host, status) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | label_format status=`{{ if hasPrefix "BLOCKED" .reason }}Blocked{{ else }}Allowed{{ end }}` [$__range])))

panels.title: Noisiest clients
panels.description: Ranked by total queries. NOT affected by the client filter — this is the panel you pick a client from.

targets.expr: sort_desc(topk(15, sum by (client_name) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` [$__range]))))

panels.title: Most-blocked clients
panels.description: Ranked by blocked queries only. Also ignores the client filter. A device near the top of this and not the panel to its left is doing little else.

targets.expr: sort_desc(topk(15, sum by (client_name) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} |= "BLOCKED" | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | reason =~ `BLOCKED.*` [$__range]))))

panels.title: Block rate by client
panels.description: Blocked as a share of that client's own queries — the third view of the same row: how many, how many blocked, and how heavily. Clients with 20 or fewer queries in the range are excluded, because one blocked query out of two is 50% and would otherwise top the chart. Ignores the client filter, like the two panels beside it.

targets.expr: sort_desc(topk(15, (sum by (client_name) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} |= "BLOCKED" | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | reason =~ `BLOCKED.*` [$__range])) / sum by (client_name) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` [$__range])) * 100) and (sum by (client_name) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` [$__range])) > 20)))

panels.title: Queries per client over time
panels.description: The top 5 clients at each point in time, bucketed. This is the panel that shows a device that started talking at 3am and has not stopped.

targets.expr: topk(5, sum by (client_name) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` [$__auto])))

panels.title: Top blocked domains
panels.description: What the blocklists are actually catching, in the range.

targets.expr: sort_desc(topk(20, sum by (question) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} |= "BLOCKED" | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason =~ `BLOCKED.*` [$__range]))))

panels.title: Top allowed domains
panels.description: What the house actually resolves, blocked queries excluded.

targets.expr: sort_desc(topk(20, sum by (question) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason !~ `BLOCKED.*` [$__range]))))

panels.title: Blocklist rules doing the work
panels.description: The matched rule rather than the domain — `ads: *.doubleclick.net` is one rule catching many names. Useful for spotting which list earns its place, and for finding the rule to allowlist when something legitimate breaks.

targets.expr: sort_desc(topk(15, sum by (rule) (count_over_time({job="blocky", host=~"$host"} |= "BLOCKED" | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` | reason =~ `BLOCKED.*` | label_format rule=`{{ regexReplaceAll "^BLOCKED \\((.*)\\)$" .reason "${1}" }}` [$__range]))))

panels.title: Query log
panels.description: The raw query log, reformatted to one readable line. Use the client box and the blocked/allowed picker at the top to narrow it.

targets.expr: {job="blocky", host=~"$host"} | pattern "<_>	<client_ip>	<client_name>	<duration_ms>	<reason>	<question>	<_>" | label_format client_name=`{{ .client_name | trimSuffix ".home.theshire.io" | trimSuffix ".theshire.io" }}` | client_name =~ `(?i).*$client.*` $logfilter | line_format `{{ .client_name }}  {{ .question }}  {{ .reason }}  {{ .duration_ms }}ms`

options.content:
**Source.** Blocky's own query log, shipped to Loki by Alloy (`modules/alloy.nix`).
Retention is Loki's 14 days, not Blocky's 30 on disk.

**The two resolvers are independent.** mirkwood and rivendell each log what
*they* answered. A client configured with both is counted in both, so `All`
sums rather than de-duplicates. Pick a single host for exact per-resolver
numbers.

**Only the left-hand columns are parsed, on purpose.** The log is tab-separated,
but the `answer` column is CSV-quoted and can itself contain tabs — an HTTPS/SVCB
record serialises with them. Parsing positionally past `answer` therefore
mis-assigns columns on ~1.5% of lines (it reads `IN` as the response type). Every
query here stops at `question`, which is lossless. Query type and response code
live past that break: get them from the **Blocky** dashboard, which reads
Prometheus.

**Client names are shortened to the bare hostname.** Blocky logs the FQDN it
gets back from the UDM Pro, so every query here runs
`| label_format client_name=...` to trim `.home.theshire.io` (and the plain
`.theshire.io` that orthanc answers with). It is a `trimSuffix`, not a cut at
the first dot, so an IPv4 address, an IPv6 address and a dotless name all pass
through untouched — which matters, because an unresolved client IS its IP here.

**Client filter** is a case-insensitive substring — `ipad` matches `iPad`. It
runs after the shortening, so it sees short names and cannot match the domain.
The three client ranking panels deliberately ignore it, so there is always
something to pick from.

**A client shown as a bare IP has no PTR, and stays that way for an hour.**
Blocky caches the client name for one hardcoded hour whether the lookup
succeeded or not, so a single failure names that device by its IP for the next
hour of log lines — which is why one device appears under both names on the
same day. The usual cause is two devices sharing a hostname: UniFi keeps one
record per name, so of three iPads only the one that renewed last has a PTR.
Renaming them is the fix, and it also splits them apart here, where all three
are a single bar. Infrastructure and tailnet addresses are pinned in
`clientLookup.clients` in `modules/dns.nix` instead, which skips the lookup.

**Every ranked panel is sorted high to low in LogQL, not in Grafana.** Loki
returns series in arbitrary order, so each of those queries is wrapped in
`sort_desc(...)` and the panel simply renders them in the order Loki hands
back. They are also set to "All values" rather than "Calculate", which draws
one bar per series instead of collapsing them to a single number.

**Do not add a `reduce` transformation to sort these instead.** An instant
query returns one frame per series carrying `meta.type: numeric-multi`, and
`reduce` spreads that meta onto its own reshaped output. The frame then lies
about its shape, the panel finds no numeric field, and every bar renders as
no-value — silently, with no error. That shipped once and looked like the
panels were reporting zero.

**Counts are queries, not devices.** A page load is many queries, and a client
that retries a blocked name inflates its own bar — which is the honest number
for "who is making the most requests", but not for "who is busiest".

list.name: client
list.label: client contains
list.description: Case-insensitive substring. Leave empty for all.

list.name: logfilter
list.label: query log shows
list.query: All : | reason =~ `.*`,Blocked only : | reason =~ `BLOCKED.*`,Allowed only : | reason !~ `BLOCKED.*`
